messages:
Alex Chen: Quick question from my trip to Berlin. Hotel put a \u20ac200 pre-authorization hold on my personal card at check-in because the Redwood corp card failed to pre-auth. At checkout they only charged \u20ac120 for room + minibar, but the \u20ac200 hold is still showing as pending on my bank. Should I submit an expense for the \u20ac120 or the full \u20ac200? And how do we handle the hold being released (bank says it can take 5-10 business days).
Maria Gomez: Thanks for flagging. Short answer: submit an expense only for the actual charged amount (\u20ac120) with the itemized folio/receipt. Refundable holds are not reimbursed. We treat holds as temporary; they should drop off the card once released by the hotel. Finance does not reimburse pending holds unless they convert to a posted charge.
Alex Chen: Got it. I can attach the folio and checkout receipt. Do you want the bank screenshot showing the pending hold too, or is the hotel's folio enough?
Sam J: Please include both if possible. The hotel folio + final invoice proves the business charge; the bank screenshot helps us track any stray holds that don't fall off. If the hold doesn't clear after 14 business days, escalate and we'll work with Travel Ops to contact the hotel.
Alex Chen: Uploads: folio link https://drive.redwood/travel/folio-171980, checkout receipt screenshot attached. I also have the bank pending hold screenshot. One weird thing: front desk gave me a receipt with a different total (\u20ac125) for incidental adjustments, but the folio shows \u20ac120. Which amount do I claim?
Travel Ops: Usually claim the posted hotel invoice amount. If there's a discrepancy, add a 1-2 sentence note explaining the front desk receipt vs folio; we may request a corrected folio from the hotel. If the hotel can provide a corrected final invoice we prefer that for audit.
Maria Gomez: Exactly. For now, submit expense for \u20ac120 (hotel charge) and attach both receipts plus a short note: "Corp card pre-auth failed, personal card used for incidentals. Hotel hold \u20ac200 pending; posted charge \u20ac120." Tag as "travel - lodging" and set currency to EUR so the automation picks it up.
Alex Chen: Thanks. One more: If the hold clears at \u20ac200 and then the hotel posts \u20ac120, will I see two transactions? Will finance reimburse \u20ac120 and ignore the released hold? I don't want to be double-paid or left with a pending block on my personal card for long.
Sam J: Good question. Banks usually release the hold and it disappears (no separate transaction). If somehow the hotel charges the full \u20ac200, you'll end up with a \u20ac200 posted charge and \u20ac120 hotel invoice discrepancy 96 in that case submit both docs and we'll reimburse the actual posted charge, then coordinate with Travel Ops to chase a refund from the hotel for any overcharge. Finance will not reimburse more than the documented posted charge.
Finance Bot: Policy excerpt: "Refundable pre-authorizations (hotel holds) are not reimbursable. Reimbursement is for actual posted charges only. If corporate card pre-auth fails and personal card is used, attach folio, posted receipt, bank statement screenshot showing posted charge, and a short explanation. If holds remain >14 business days, escalate to Travel Ops for vendor engagement." Link: https://intranet.redwood/fin/travel-holds
Alex Chen: Submitting expense now with folio + bank screenshot + note. Appreciate the quick guidance :thumbsup:
Maria Gomez: Will review once submitted. If the hotel can issue a corrected folio we may ask you to attach it, but this looks straightforward. Thanks for including the bank screenshot.
